01 · What I bring

What changes in your company

Four things I have done before and would do for you. Each one is backed by the story below.

  1. A clear picture of how the business really runs

    I map how work, people, data and money connect, and then redesign the parts that slow everyone down.

    At Silpo, store managers could see the part of their store's P&L they control by the 5th of the following month.

  2. Projects that get finished and keep working

    I have run cross-functional and strategic projects, built a project office and trained project managers. After launch I write the results into standards, so the gains don't slide back.

    At Silpo, while the chain grew from about 120 to 300 stores: more than 20 legal entities merged into one, acquired chains integrated, a practical project management course for retail.

  3. AI with clear rules

    In my systems one AI proposes, a second AI from another vendor checks it, and a person decides. Scripts verify the numbers. Sensitive data goes out only with explicit consent. I would bring the same rules to your teams.

    A car-audio tuning method built this way earned five competition awards in 2026, and a first place for one of its users.

  4. IT and finance in the same conversation

    I studied systems programming and worked as a CTO. I also studied business management and decision economics and served as an expert in a McKinsey operations working group. I can talk to IT and to finance without a translator.

    At Ciklum I planned and budgeted IT as CTO. At Silpo the project office planned store headcount, payroll and productivity from planned revenue.

01 · 1987–1991

Electronics

Kharkiv Technical School of Radio Electronics, with a focus on CNC machine tools: circuits, sensors and machines that do exactly what the program tells them. The habit stayed. Years later I designed the electrical, water and heating systems for my own home.

02 · 1991–1996

Software

Kharkiv Polytechnic Institute, computer science and systems programming. From 1994 I wrote software at Escape, automating retail trading systems. Retail came back into my life fourteen years later.

04 · Silpo, from 2008

Running retail operations at scale

Silpo is one of Ukraine's largest food retail chains. While I worked there it grew from about 120 to 300 stores, with around 40,000 people. I joined to run the IT office and later built and led the project management office.

Director of the IT office

2008–2012 · reporting to the executive director
  • Standards, checklists and procedures for regional IT teams that support the stores.
  • Store processes described; document flow between stores and offices put in order, with a new records department.
  • Labour standards for store work.
  • Staff and checkout schedules planned in half-hour slots from customer traffic.
  • Queue alerts sent to store managers and supervisors by SMS.
  • More than 20 operating legal entities merged into one.

Director of the project management office

From 2012 · reporting to the COO
  • Annual planning and budgeting of store and production headcount, payroll and productivity, driven by store format, processes and planned revenue.
  • Store P&L: the costs a store manager controls became visible by the 5th of the following month.
  • A KPI system based on the balanced scorecard, from a single store to the whole chain: weekly for corrections, monthly to yearly for targets and bonuses.
  • Restructuring: legal entities merged, stores moved between entities, acquired chains integrated.
  • Expert in a McKinsey working group on operational processes.
  • A mobile platform for store processes. One annual stocktake instead of monthly ones.
  • Built and taught a practical project management course for retail.

These results describe the work as it was done at the time. The company's systems have changed since.

05 · Now

Applied AI

I am one of two partners at FlipManager, a startup building an AI exoskeleton for managers: digital assistants that take routine off people and support them in their daily work. We are developing four products on one shared base:

  • DPA, a digital personal assistant for one person.
  • DBA, an assistant for a small business owner.
  • DPC, a personal assistant for managers inside a company.
  • DCC, Digital Company Compass, a compass for the company as a whole.

We started from both ends. I build the assistants for a person and for a small business owner. My partner is working on security at enterprise level.

Alongside that, I build my own AI systems from start to finish. That is where I find out what works before I recommend it to anyone. One of them is a car-audio tuning method, and it needed every earlier chapter: electronics, software, project discipline and, now, AI.

03 · AI in practice

Projects you can check

Two public projects of my own and one FlipManager product in development. In each, several AI models have separate roles, tests catch mistakes, and a person makes the final call. Real users and competition results check the outcome.

Public

Autosound Tuning Skill

View on GitHub ↗

A Claude skill that guides the tuning of a car's sound processor from real measurements. Claude proposes crossovers, delays and equalisation. A second AI from another vendor reviews each round and is not allowed to praise. The person listens and decides. The tool never changes the processor by itself.

120+releases since June 2026
68test queries that check when the skill should and shouldn't start
4languages of method and docs

Results in 2026: my own car won five awards at EMMA and AYA championships, including two first places and third at the German EMMA Final. A user's car took first place at the AYA Finale.

Public

Autosound TCC

View on GitHub ↗

A desktop app for macOS and Windows that puts the same method on screen: live measurements, the predicted result, the plan, and an AI panel. AI agents work through 36 tools that the app exposes, and every change still needs the person's approval.

4,300+automated tests
36tools for AI agents
3platforms in CI, signed releases
Private · FlipManager

Digital Personal Assistant (DPA)

Ask for a demo ↓

The FlipManager product I am building first. An assistant for someone who runs many projects at once. Each project keeps its own space, and one overview shows what is happening across all of them. It saves its state as it goes, transcribes meetings on my own computer, and asks a second AI for an independent opinion. Nothing goes to an outside model without my explicit "yes".
